title: Cueworkbench Scraps - Microtemplates & Failure Triage
body:
Quick notes, experiments, and oddball failures while I iterate on the "Cueworkbench" microtemplate set. Mostly raw thinking + tiny examples so I don't forget patterns.

Goal: build a compact set of 3–5 microtemplates that can be combined at request time to produce stable, controllable responses for UI helper flows (error explanations, rewrite suggestions, short examples). Prioritize token budget (<= 120 tokens overhead).

1) Microtemplate sketches (one-liners)
- intent-clarify: "User intent: {{short_user_input}}. Ask a single clarifying question if ambiguous, otherwise proceed."
- safe-summary: "Condense to one sentence, avoid technical jargon, and flag any potential policy concerns."
- actionable-stepper: "Return 2–3 concrete next steps the user can take, numbered."

2) Few-shot combos (quick trials)
- Template: [instruction] + [fewshot examples x2] + [user prompt] + [system guard]
- Fewshot example A (rewrite):
  input: "My code crashes when I click save"
  output: "Try checking console for X, confirm network, attach stack trace."
- Fewshot example B (explain):
  input: "App shows 500 on submit"
  output: "500 indicates server error; try re-trying, check service logs for stack traces, include request id."

3) Observed brittle cases (failure triage log)
- Case F1: directive collapse when user utterance includes multiple ambiguous cues ("I tried saving but now login doesn't work") -> model ignores login issue and focuses on save. Notes: add explicit instruction to enumerate separate problems and ask which to prioritize.
- Case F2: hallucinated debug hints (model invents a logger name from nonexistent stacktrace) -> mitigation: include 'never invent file/class names' guard and require quoting of any identifiers present in input.
- Case F3: token bloat in fewshot chain: model repeats example paraphrase leading to +80 tokens. Mitigation: shorter exemplars, switch to <condensed> markers, or compress examples with placeholders.

4) Small experiments to run (quick A/B list)
- E1: Compare 1 vs 2 fewshots for rewrite tasks at temp=0.2, measure % of answers that mention exact steps (manual label n=50).
- E2: Add explicit 'if ambiguous, list clarifying questions only' line vs 'ask one clarifying question', watch for multiplicity.
- E3: Try token-budget constraint: append 'Respond in <= 70 tokens' and measure truncation vs quality.

5) Useful guard phrases (to copy into templates)
- "Do not invent names, IDs, stack traces, or file paths. If missing, say 'not provided'."
- "List problems separately; do not conflate multiple issues into one paragraph."
- "If you need clarifying info, ask only one question unless the user specifically asks for more."

6) Example brittle transcript (raw)
- USER: "I tried updating the profile picture, now my account is locked and emails bounce"
- MODEL: (bad) "Sounds like your email bounces because of SMTP settings; check server auth." -> incorrect assumption, ignores lockout.
- INTERVENTION: prepend 'When multiple problems are reported, list them in bullets and ask which to prioritize.'

7) Open questions / TODOs
- Q1: Are we ok with a small set of negative exemplars (showing what not to do), or do negative examples add noise? Samir thinks negatives help for hallucination mitigation.
- Q2: How to best surface a single 'confidence' metric in the fewshot examples—model-rated or heuristic?
- TODO: run E1 and E3 this week; ping Jin for labeling help; add results to ENG-6142.

8) Snippets to try in console (copy friendly)
- Instruction header (compact): "You are a concise assistant for developer-facing help. Follow the guard lines below. Be concise."
- Guard block: "GUARDS:
1) Do not invent specifics. 2) If multiple issues, bullet them. 3) Prefer numbered actions (max 3)."
- Example payload (JSONish): {user_input: "site throws 502 after deploy", context: "deploy id d-983, started 10:34am"}

Notes to self: keep exemplars to 1–2 sentence outputs; prefer active verbs; test on hosted API with dedicated quantized-small model and also on private infra to observe any quantization artifacts (repetition, truncated punctuation). Save winning microtemplate combos as: micro-v1 / micro-v1a / micro-v2.

End of scraps. Random thought: try 'ensemble micro' where 2 microtemplates run and outputs are merged deterministically (merge rules: prefer shorter, prefer containing numbers).
